c.st: Use Cases for Change-Class in Common Lisp

CLOS class instances are implemented with handles for a very important reason: so slots can be added to classes dynamically, even if live instances exist.

In decades of Common Lisp programming I think I've written a CHANGE-CLASS call maybe twice, but I add slots to classes all the time (and occasionally remove them).

c.st: Use Cases for Change-Class in Common Lisp
c.x: Right. The two things are different despite having the same ultimate effect, since (in the context of Common Lisp) one is a generic operation provided by the language, while the other is application-specific with no language support and would need a fragile bespoke implementation for every single use. If the discussion was about Smalltalk that provides become: but not CHANGE-CLASS, it'd be a different question.
